top_stances.summary: Wants to restore recently-cut ACA subsidies and SNAP benefits, require 100% federal Medicaid funding, and build a long-term universal basic income floor.
Would expand mobile clinics, credential private doctors into the VA network to cut out insurers, negotiate drug prices at the lowest federal rate paid.
Proposes a Florida co-op factory building hurricane-rated, expandable modular homes on standard mortgages, with ownership modeled on Publix or a credit union.
Wants to restore the 30% solar tax credit, add home battery storage, and make data centers fund their own grid upgrades to cut reliance on imported gas.
Wants to guarantee affordable health care for every American, prevent medical bankruptcy, and double the behavioral health workforce to cut wait times.
Supports raising the corporate tax rate to the Reagan-era 26% and closing stock-compensation loopholes to fund social programs.
Backs a new tax on corporate home purchases plus incentives for affordable construction, saying homes should be lived in, not traded as assets.
Would cap federal student loan interest at 3.1% and provide universal free school lunch for public school students.

candidates.name: Troy Albers
candidates.bio: Troy Albers is a Democratic candidate for Florida's 3rd Congressional District. He served in the U.S. Navy, the Florida National Guard, and later the U.S. Army, and became a farmer after leaving the military. He says he is running for people who are tired of being ignored, for families doing everything right and still falling behind, and for rural communities that feel forgotten.
key_messages: Treat health insurance as a cost-of-living issue: lower out-of-pocket costs and stop insurers standing between families and their doctors
Pass the Neighborhood Homes Investment Act to build lower-cost housing in underserved communities
Vote no on eliminating property taxes, because cities and counties need them to pay for services
Bring emergency care closer to rural North Central Florida as rural hospitals close
Oppose new data centers, which consume more resources than the value they produce

campaign_themes.heading: Economy
campaign_themes.text: Families should not have to work harder every year just to fall further behind. High unemployment combined with high inflation is choking the economy, and people are working harder to get less. Government should focus on lowering the pressure on working people, strengthening opportunity, and rewarding real work instead of accepting a country where basic stability feels out of reach.

campaign_themes.heading: Health insurance
campaign_themes.text: Health insurance should help people get care, not stand between families and their doctors. Too many Americans pay more every year for premiums, deductibles, prescriptions and surprise bills while still wondering whether the care they need will actually be covered. Congress should treat health insurance as a cost-of-living issue: protect access to care, lower out-of-pocket costs, fight waste and abuse in the system, and make sure insurance companies serve patients instead of trapping them in paperwork and denial.

campaign_themes.heading: Healthcare and rural hospitals
campaign_themes.text: Affordable care should be within reach for ordinary Americans, not a constant financial gamble. Rural hospitals are closing one after another, which leaves people driving over an hour to get care. Rural families deserve faster, more reliable access to emergency care close to home. Wants to explore practical infrastructure solutions, including adding helipads to fire stations in key areas, so rural North Central Florida has better emergency access when local care is too far away or unavailable.

campaign_themes.heading: Housing affordability
campaign_themes.text: Supports the federal government passing the Neighborhood Homes Investment Act, which would create a tax incentive for developers, builders, and local governments to build lower-cost housing in eligible underserved communities.

campaign_themes.heading: Property and auto insurance
campaign_themes.text: Florida leads the nation in the cost of property insurance and is second in the nation for the cost of automobile insurance, to the point where people cannot afford insurance. Homeowners watch premiums climb, renters feel those costs passed down, and drivers pay more just to stay legal on the road. Florida needs real accountability in the insurance market, stronger consumer protection, smarter policies that cut bureaucratic waste, and a serious push from every level of government to make property and auto insurance more stable, more transparent and more affordable for Floridians.

campaign_themes.heading: Property taxes
campaign_themes.text: A no vote on the constitutional amendment to eliminate property taxes. Cities and counties need property taxes to pay for the services they provide citizens; he does not like paying them either, but there is no answer to how a county or city funds services without them.

campaign_themes.heading: Utilities and data centers
campaign_themes.text: A firm no on data centers, which consume more resources than the value they produce for society. Utility companies need to find ways to produce energy without burning something.

campaign_themes.heading: Environment and climate
campaign_themes.text: The government should do more regarding climate change. As he puts it, the Earth is our landlord, and if we do not make the changes to help our landlord, we could face eviction. Wildlife conservation is about safety and stewardship, not just scenery; supports wildlife crossings in high-conflict corridors around Paynes Prairie and similar areas to reduce collisions while protecting the landscape.

campaign_themes.heading: Federal spending and oversight
campaign_themes.text: The people deserve a government that treats public money with discipline and respect. Reckless spending and weak accountability have damaged trust across multiple administrations and left taxpayers holding the bill. Congress should demand real transparency and exercise stronger oversight, including serious civilian scrutiny of executive and military power, and remember that every dollar spent belongs to the people first.

campaign_themes.heading: Climate change
campaign_themes.text: The government should do more regarding climate change. As he puts it, the Earth is our landlord, and if we do not make the changes to help our landlord, we could face eviction.

campaign_themes.heading: Wildlife and conservation
campaign_themes.text: Wildlife conservation is about safety and stewardship, not just scenery. Supports wildlife crossings in high-conflict corridors around Paynes Prairie and similar areas to reduce collisions while protecting the landscape.

Support Neighborhood Homes Investment Act to create tax incentives for building lower-cost housing in underserved communities.
Lower pressure on working people by addressing inflation, unemployment, and wage stagnation; strengthen opportunity and reward real work.
Government should do more on climate change; Earth is our landlord and we must make changes to avoid eviction.
Support wildlife crossings in high-conflict corridors to reduce collisions and protect landscape; conservation is stewardship and safety.
Firmly oppose data centers; they consume more resources than the value they produce for society.
Demand real transparency and stronger congressional oversight of spending and executive/military power; treat public money with discipline.
Bring emergency care closer to rural areas through practical infrastructure solutions like adding helipads to fire stations.
